feed.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack

entry.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
entry.summary:
Optimizing implementations remains beneficial even when adjustments to stack size are considered, suggesting that such optimizations ought to be pursued as a general practice. In relation to opcode blacklisting, specifically concerning the `OP_DUP` operation, imposing a restriction where `OP_DUP` is limited to duplicating elements up to 520 bytes introduces an alternative approach. The same outcome could be achieved by mandating that the witness includes the relevant stack element twice, followed by utilizing `OP_EQUAL`, thereby shifting the cost of increased transaction size onto the spender.
The constraints on the stack size that an opcode can manipulate are already established within Bitcoin’s scripting system. Push operations and several mathematical opcodes are subject to these limitations. Introducing a size limit for `OP_DUP` aligns with this existing framework and could serve as a practical compromise, balancing script functionality with resource management.
